note: Study skeleton paraphrased from the course scope (not verbatim College Board prose; unit numbers are our own sequencing, not official CED numbers). Skill codes are indicative: 1.x concept, 2.x/3.x skill. Shared framework: all AP world language & culture courses use the same three communication modes and six cultural themes.

objectives.statement: Explain strategies for understanding articles, audio, and video in the target language.
Interpret authentic texts and media, identifying main ideas and supporting details.
Explain how conversation, debate, and correspondence negotiate meaning between speakers.
Sustain spontaneous conversations and written exchanges with appropriate register.
Explain how to structure cultural comparisons and persuasive presentations for an audience.
Deliver organized spoken and written presentations with cultural evidence.
Explain family structures and community life across cultures.
Compare attitudes toward family and community in discussions and essays.
Explain how language, heritage, and belonging shape identity.
Discuss identity topics using culturally appropriate expression.
Explain ideals of beauty and artistic expression across cultures.
Analyze cultural products and their aesthetic values.
Explain how technology and science affect daily life and communication.
Debate technology's effects using evidence from target-language sources.
Explain education, work, leisure, and travel in target cultures.
Compare daily life across cultures in speech and writing.
Explain environmental, health, and economic challenges from multiple perspectives.
Propose and defend responses to a global issue with sourced evidence.
